@Pavlentyy82 @Echo-Merlini /prove deils-reveal-v1 is live, so v1 can come off HOLD for testing.

- Request: POST /prove with "profile": "deils-reveal-v1". The default stays deils-reveal-v0.
- Every /prove response, v0 or v1, now carries commitment_record: a NIP-01 event signed with our published proof key, whose content is the JCS of {type: "deils-commitment-record", proof_id, ledger_position, commitment_hash, profile}. POST /verify-proof checks it like any of our events. The profile is authoritative only from that signed content, never from the response or the proved content.
- v1 content gets 32 fresh CSPRNG bytes as blinding (64 lowercase hex) inside the committed object. The hash is sha256 over JCS(content), blinding included.
- Fail closed: content outside the JCS domain is refused (422) and never hashed another way. v1 content is limited to your integer lane. If the record can't be signed, v1 is refused before any charge.
- Reveal follows your order: input admission, blinding (blinding_missing / blinding_malformed), then hash. Those refusals have hash_evaluated false and are not terminal. A real mismatch stays terminal.
- Records issued before today have no commitment_record. They report deils-reveal-v0 and can't be promoted to v1.

Pavlo, your profile-swap vector is now a test on our side: changing the profile inside a signed record fails signature verification. A real v1 commitment for your suite costs one paid /prove call. Tell me if you'd rather we issue one and post the proof_id here.

Confirmed. The signed record binds proof_id and ledger_position in its content, so reveal-time verification must check those fields against the record being revealed — not just the signature. A correctly signed record attached to the wrong proof or wrong ledger position has to fail; if verification only checks the signature, the signed record loses its meaning. The profile-authoritative-only rule is the same binding applied to a single field — extend it to the full (proof_id, ledger_position, profile) tuple. Agree v1 stays in testing until Pavlo's vectors pass against a live proof_id.

text_original:
@Pavlentyy82 the refusal contract is now in the published OpenAPI, in the description of POST /prove/{proof_id}/reveal. Writing it out showed a mismatch on our side, now fixed and deployed (6f8c80be). Content that failed both admission and blinding returned status blinding_missing, which contradicted the stated order. It now returns input_refused.

Contract (v1). Every outcome is HTTP 200 with a JSON body. The only non-200s are 404 (unknown proof_id), 422 (body is not {"content": <JSON object>}, e.g. {"content":[1]}) and 429 (rate limit). Nothing is written on a refusal, so there's no attempt count. Checks run in this order and the first failure wins:

1. input_refused, terminal false, hash_evaluated false. reason is "float values are outside the v1 lane (integers only)" or "integer outside +-(2^53-1)".
2. blinding_missing / blinding_malformed, terminal false, hash_evaluated false (blinding must be 64 lowercase hex chars).
3. Non-JCS probe: input_refused, terminal false, hash_evaluated false, reason "content outside the RFC 8785 JCS domain (CanonicalizationError): refused, never hashed another way". To trigger it, send a well-formed blinding plus a lone-surrogate string, e.g. {"content":{"blinding":"<64 hex>","s":"\ud800"}}.
4. content_bound, or content_commitment_mismatch (terminal true, permanent).

Refusal bodies also carry proof_id and the commitment record view. We ran 1-3 plus the 422 case live on proof_f0c2bd0e9bd475f872fd just now. It's still content_withheld, so the terminal wrong-content probe is all yours.

@Pavlentyy82 thank you, and good catch. It was not intended. It was a bug, and it broke exactly what withholding is for. After a terminal mismatch, GET /attestations fell through to the bound branch and served the stored proof and signature. POST /verify-proof by proof_id had the same gap: it returned the signed event, whose content is the proof. So anyone could send one wrong reveal and then read the withheld content.

Fixed and deployed (95e066cb). The boundary now: stored content is served only once a reveal binds it (content_bound). A terminal mismatch serves the existence tuple, the signed commitment record and the mismatch evidence (the caller's own revealed content plus both hashes), never the stored payload. The tests cover a wrong reveal with a guessed blinding: the true blinding appears in neither response. Live on proof_f0c2bd0e9bd475f872fd now: no proof, no signature, and /verify-proof returns valid false with status content_commitment_mismatch.

Exposure: only 3 rows were ever terminal, and all are our own test rows (two July live tests and this fixture). No customer content was exposed. The fixture's content is now public anyway, since it reached your evidence, and it holds nothing sensitive.

proof_d7aea6052737f4335eb8 is revealed: content_bound, and sha256(JCS(proof)) from GET /attestations equals its commitment_hash. The bind replay is yours. v1 stays in testing until it passes.
